title: Pressure Cooker Beef Stew
description: A rich, savoury beef, potato and carrot stew with tomatoes, onion, garlic, fish sauce and Vietnamese stock powder. Made in a stovetop pressure cooker.

ingredients.name: beef
ingredients.note: cut into large chunks; nạm bò or bắp bò work well

ingredients.name: fish sauce
ingredients.note: optional, to adjust seasoning after cooking

steps.text: Heat the oil in the open pressure cooker. Sauté the chopped onion for about 1–2 minutes until it starts to soften; add the garlic for the last 30–60 seconds, avoiding burning it.
Add beef and brown for 6–8 minutes, turning occasionally to develop colour.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook for 3–5 minutes, until they soften and begin to break down.
Add fish sauce, soy sauce, stock powder, MSG, sugar, black pepper and 350–400 ml water. Stir and scrape any browned bits off the base.
Place potato and carrot chunks on top. Close and lock the pressure cooker lid.

On the induction hob, use about 2000 W to reach full pressure. Reduce to the lowest setting that keeps full pressure (often around 600–800 W with gentle regulator movement). Start the 25-minute timer once full pressure is reached.
Turn the heat off. Let the cooker depressurize naturally for 10 minutes, then carefully release any remaining pressure according to its instructions before opening.
Stir and taste. If needed, add up to 1 tsp extra fish sauce; taste again. Serve with rice or bread.

notes: This is the tomato-and-onion version; not the later no-tomato batch scaled for 430 g beef.
Chunky vegetables cooked for 25 minutes will be soft. For firmer potatoes and carrots, pressure cook the beef first, then add vegetables and pressure cook about 4 more minutes.
Watt settings vary by cooker; maintain pressure based on your cooker’s regulator and instructions rather than relying on a fixed watt number.
